opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Andrew Mann (E014) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role; as full-time, maximum is write (admin only if role owns system). Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Andrew Mann (E014) is a contractor with basic training (note earlier said full-time). Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: Andrew Mann (E014) requests write access to Payroll. HR's note says full-time Payroll Specialist (max write for full-time employees), but Security's note says the Security DB shows contractor with basic training (max read for contractors without advanced security training). The employment records conflict. Applying the more restrictive/security-verified classification (contractor, basic training), the maximum permitted level is read. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Andrew Mann (E014), requesting write access to Payroll.

There are conflicting notes:
- HR note: full_time Payroll Specialist, recommends write.
- Security note: contractor, basic training, recommends read.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The two notes conflict on employment type. HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

According to policy, contractors with basic training max out at read. Full-time max is write (admin only if role owns system). Requested write.

The conflicting facts matter. Which to trust? As Approver, I need to make a decision. The Security agent notes the discrepancy and recommends read. Typically, in these scenarios, the more restrictive/security-based note should prevail. The Security agent's DB says contractor with basic training, so max is read.

Given the conflict, the safe decision is read (the maximum for a contractor with basic training), and grant the maximum if requested above. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.

Evidence: HR note says full-time Payroll Specialist (max write for full-time; admin only if role owns system); Security note says contractor with basic training (max read). Conflicting employment records; Security DB indicates contractor with basic training, so maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, grant read.
